Definition: to occupy (by driving out previous tenants, and possessing in their place); by implication, to seize, to rob, to inherit; also to expel, to impoverish, to ruin
BiblicalUsage: 1) to seize, dispossess, take possession off, inherit, disinherit, occupy, impoverish, be an heir; 1a) (Qal); 1a1) to take possession of; 1a2) to inherit; 1a3) to impoverish, come to poverty, be poor; 1b) (Niphal) to be dispossessed, be impoverished, come to poverty; 1c) (Piel) to devour; 1d) (Hiphil); 1d1) to cause to possess or inherit; 1d2) to cause others to possess or inherit; 1d3) to impoverish; 1d4) to dispossess; 1d5) to destroy, bring to ruin, disinherit
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
